security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel code treats the entire aclicsourcecfg[0] indirect register as read-only zero (e.g., skipping save/restore of xireg2/xireg3 when xiselect=0x1000, or writing zero to all 32/64 bits expecting it to be ignored), when in fact only bits [15:0] (sourcecfg[0][15:0]) are read-only zero — the upper bits map to live sourcecfg[1] (XLEN=32) or sourcecfg[1..3] (XLEN=64) and control real interrupt source configuration.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: "xiselect.*0x1000" OR "xireg[23].*read.only.zero" OR "aclicsourcecfg.*zero" OR "sourcecfg\[0\].*zero" AND NOT "\[15:0\]" — code that assumes full-register read-only-zero semantics for indirect sourcecfg[0] access instead of the partial [15:0]-only zeroing corrected in this PR.
security_spec.summary: FreeBSD does not yet implement ACLIC/Smidctrl indirect CSR access, but if/when it does, code must treat only aclicsourcecfg[0][15:0] as read-only zero — not the full register — to avoid corrupting source configuration for interrupts 1–3 (XLEN=64) or interrupt 1 (XLEN=32) that share the same xireg2/xireg3 window.

findings.finding: APLIC driver explicitly rejects IMSIC-based configurations ('APLIC with IMSIC is unsupported'), meaning the AIA indirect CSR mechanism (siselect/sireg for aclicsourcecfg) is never exercised. No code in this file accesses CSR-based indirect registers.

CSR definitions for SISELECT (0x150) and SIREG (0x151) are entirely absent from encoding.h. No AIA indirect-register CSR constants exist, confirming the kernel has zero code capable of accessing aclicsourcecfg[] via the xiselect/xireg indirect mechanism.

VMM hypcsr structure saves/restores only basic supervisor CSRs (hvip, vsstatus, vsie, vstvec, vsscratch, vsepc, vscause, vstval, vsatp, scounteren, senvcfg). No vsiselect/vsireg or siselect/sireg fields exist, which is consistent with the VMM's lack of AIA support. The vulnerability condition (misinterpreting aclicsourcecfg[0] layout) cannot occur because no guest-visible AIA indirect CSR path exists.

VMM CSR save/restore only covers the CSRs listed in hypcsr. No siselect/sireg or vsiselect/vsireg save/restore is performed, which is safe because the VMM does not expose AIA indirect CSR functionality to guests.

VMM APLIC emulation handles only MMIO-mapped APLIC registers (domaincfg, sourcecfg per-IRQ words, target, IDC delivery/claim/etc.). It does not emulate CSR-based AIA indirect register access (siselect/sireg). The sourcecfg[] array entries are per-IRQ MMIO words with standard AIA sourcecfg semantics, unrelated to the CSR-based aclicsourcecfg indirect register layout issue.

The VMM world-switch assembly does not save/restore siselect, sireg, vsiselect, or vsireg. This is consistent with the VMM's lack of AIA indirect CSR support and therefore does not violate the spec — there is no code that could misinterpret aclicsourcecfg[0] semantics.
